blocks.text: The valves have to open and close at exactly the right moment, every cycle, thousands of times a minute. Nobody flips them by hand. A spinning shaft called the **camshaft** does it.
The camshaft has egg-shaped bumps called **cams**. As it spins, each bump pushes its valve open, then lets a spring snap it shut.
Why the cam turns at half speed

Each valve opens **once per cycle**. One cycle is **two** crank turns. So the camshaft has to turn **once** while the crankshaft turns **twice**. A belt or chain links them, and the cam gear has **twice as many teeth** as the crank gear.

blocks.caption: Top: the crank gear (20 teeth) drives the cam gear (40 teeth). Bottom: one full cam turn, which is one whole cycle.
blocks.narration: Watch the counters. Every time the crankshaft finishes two turns, the camshaft finishes exactly one.

lines: So the cam turns 1 time for every 2 crank turns
blocks.say: Forty teeth divided by twenty teeth is two. So the cam turns once for every two turns of the crank.

blocks.text: In a textbook engine each valve opens exactly at the top or bottom. Real engines open them **early** and close them **late**. Moving air has momentum, like water in a hose. Keeping the intake open a bit past the bottom lets the rushing air keep cramming in.

Around the top, between exhaust and intake, **both valves are open at once** for a moment. That's called **valve overlap**. The exhaust rushing out helps pull the fresh mix in behind it. Flip the lab to **Real** to see it.

Burning isn't instant. It takes a couple of thousandths of a second. So the spark fires **before** the top. That way the pressure peaks just **after** the top, right when it can push the piston down best. Engineers call this **spark advance**.

blocks.title: Why faster means earlier
blocks.text: The burn always takes about the same time. But at higher RPM the crank turns further during that time, so the spark has to fire earlier. Drag the **RPM** slider and watch the ⚡ mark move.

lines: A 2 ms burn = 2 × 18° = 36° of crank turn
blocks.say: Three thousand R P M is fifty turns a second, so one turn takes twenty milliseconds. That's eighteen degrees every millisecond. A two millisecond burn means the crank turns thirty six degrees while the fuel is still burning.

blocks.question: The camshaft turns at what speed compared with the crankshaft?
blocks.explain: Half speed: each valve opens once per cycle, and a cycle is two crank turns.

blocks.question: What is valve overlap?
options: Both valves open for a moment near the top, between exhaust and intake
The valves bumping into the piston
The cam turning twice per cycle
blocks.explain: Near the top between exhaust and intake, both are open briefly. The outgoing exhaust helps pull in the fresh mix.

blocks.question: Why does the spark fire before the piston reaches the top?
options: Because burning takes time, so it starts early to peak just after the top
It's a mistake engines just live with
blocks.explain: The burn takes a few milliseconds. Starting early makes the pressure peak right when it can push the piston down.
